content:
**Companies that have reached a market‑capitalisation of $1 trillion or more (according to the Wikipedia “Trillion‑dollar companies” table) and the year they were founded**

| # | Company | Year founded* | Notes on the $1 T milestone |
|---|---------|--------------|-----------------------------|
| 1 | **Apple Inc.** | **1976** (Apple Computer, Inc.) | First U.S. company to break $1 T (2 Aug 2018) and later $2 T, $3 T. |
| 2 | **Microsoft Corp.** | **1975** (Micro‑Soft) | Crossed $1 T on 7 Jun 2019; later $2 T (June 2021). |
| 3 | **Saudi Aramco** (Saudi Arabian Oil Co.) | **1933** (as California‑Arabian Standard Oil Co.; renamed Saudi Aramco in 1988) | Hit $1 T on 11 Dec 2019; later $2 T (May 2022). |
| 4 | **Alphabet Inc.** (Google) | **1998** (Google founded by Larry Page & Sergey Brin) – Alphabet created as the holding company in **2015** | First passed $1 T on 16 Jan 2020; later $2 T (Nov 2021). |
| 5 | **Amazon.com, Inc.** | **1994** (launched as an online bookstore) | Reached $1 T on 4 Sep 2018; later $2 T (July 2021). |
| 6 | **Nvidia Corp.** | **1993** (founded by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, Curtis Priem) | First hit $1 T on 30 May 2023 (driven by AI‑chip demand). |

\*Founding year reflects the year the business was originally incorporated or launched. For Saudi Aramco the earliest incorporation (1933) is used, even though the modern “Saudi Aramco” name came later.

**Why these companies only**

- The Wikipedia “Trillion‑dollar companies” table lists the **only** publicly traded firms that have ever exceeded a market cap of $1 trillion.  
- Companies such as **Tesla**, **Meta Platforms**, **Berkshire Hathaway**, etc., have flirted with the $1 T mark in the past but have not sustained it (or fell below it before the most recent data).  
- As of 2025 the six companies above are the ones that have either maintained or re‑attained the $1 T threshold, making them the definitive list.
